the fallback's sandbox-local outcome is a stated residual (DFSR-FALLBACK-2), not a `RootConfig` state (the tone and `passed` never disagree); the status line over a forced-stdio probe list reads healthy with the note counted as a note). BINDING SEAM — every signature is stated HERE once; §2.1 refers to this list. )` passed; `Global` → `state_root: global` passed; `InvalidUtf8` → `state_root: RMAP_STATE_ROOT is set but is not valid UTF-8; the client ignores it (global root, or a sandbox-local root after an auto fallback)` FAILED (counted); `pub(crate) fn service_note_applies(cfg: &DoctorConfig) -> bool` — `cfg.transport == Stdio || matches!(cfg.root, RootConfig::Override(_))` (the ONE note predicate; `InvalidUtf8` is not an override — the client ignores it); `pub(crate) fn service_note_detail(cfg: &DoctorConfig) -> Option` — `Stdio` → `stdio transport configured; this service is not used by a stdio client`; otherwise `Override(p)` → `measures the global launchd service; this run's configured state root is

`; else `None`. In `platform/mod.rs`: `check_daemon_socket()`, `granular_socket_probes()`, `socket_resolution_probes()` keep their public no-argument signatures (the adapters and the Linux adapter call them unchanged) and delegate to `check_daemon_socket_with(mode: TransportMode, diag: &PathResolutionDiagnostics)`, `granular_socket_probes_with(mode, diag)`, `socket_resolution_probes_with(mode, diag)`; the public functions pass `TransportMode::from_env()` and the live diagnostics; under `Stdio` the `_with` variants return the FIVE named socket-related probes (`daemon_socket`, `socket_file`, `socket_connect`, `socket_ping`, `socket_path`) as `n/a (stdio transport)` passes without touching the socket, and `socket_resolution_probes_with` keeps its OTHER resolution probes (`effective_uid`, `env_home`, `canonical_home`, `socket_resolution`, `socket_override`) exactly as today — they are facts of path resolution, not socket probes — so the stdio JSON still totals 27 probes. In `platform/macos.rs`: `fn service_probe(status: ServiceStatus, cfg: &DoctorConfig) -> ProbeResult` (pure; `doctor_probes` passes the live `launchctl` status and `doctor_config()`): label `launchd service (global state root): `; when `service_note_applies(cfg)` → `passed = true` with `service_note_detail(cfg)` as the detail; otherwise today's pass/fail per state, no detail. In `commands/doctor/summary.rs`: `pub(super) fn apply_service_probe_tone(probes: &mut [ProbeOutput], note: bool)` — sets `daemon_service`'s tone to `Note` only when `note && passed` (a failed probe is never a note); `execute_doctor` always calls it with ONE expression on every target: `let note = cfg!(target_os = "macos") && service_note_applies(&cfg);` (`cfg!` is a plain `bool`, so the Linux library build still references and type-checks `service_note_applies` — NO `#[cfg]`-selected statements anywhere in `execute_doctor`; D-DFSR-LINUX-SCOPE-1 reserves the note rule for DFSR-LINUX-1: on Linux `note` is always `false` and a passing Linux `daemon_service` never shows `[note]`); `service_note_applies`, `apply_service_probe_tone`, `early_config_probes`, `doctor_config` and the `_with` variants are cross-platform — compiled, referenced from production code and unit-tested on both targets; ONLY `service_note_detail` and its re-export are `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]`-gated (its one consumer is the macOS adapter's `service_probe`; the re-export is its own gated `pub(crate) use doctor_config_probes::service_note_detail;` line, separate from the cross-platform `pub(crate) use` list), so Linux Clippy (`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` in CI) sees no unused item and every rgr unit test compiles on Linux. No test reads or sets the process environment: every test constructs `DoctorConfig` / `PathResolutionDiagnostics` / `ServiceStatus` / `ProbeOutput` values. PRE-CONNECTION SOURCE: `doctor_config()` above — nothing on this path depends on `DaemonClient::new()` succeeding; an absent variable (`NotPresent` → `Global`) is distinct from a malformed one (`NotUnicode` → `InvalidUtf8`, a failed probe).
